subject: Service provider role for telemetry; encryption evidence and subprocessor visibility
messages:
From: Samuel Clark <samuel.clark@brightlinehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: legal@brightlinehealth.com
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify Redwood's role for telemetry and request for encryption evidence

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal had a couple of follow-ups around the telemetry we send during inference telemetry and traces. Two specific asks we need to close before our procurement team can finalize the P.O.:

1) Role characterization: Can you confirm whether Redwood will act as a "Service Provider" (limited-use/processor equivalent) for telemetry related to Brightline requests, or whether any of those telemetry flows are considered "Operator"/sale under CA law? We need the language to appear in the DPA addendum.

2) Encryption proof: We need a short artifact that shows telemetry is encrypted in transit and at rest (diagram or short statement from infra). Ideally: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, key management details.

3) Subprocessor visibility: please provide the current subprocessor list for any infra or telemetry-handling vendors and a proposed onshore fallback timeline if there are offshore subprocessors handling identifiable telemetry.

Can you loop in whoever owns telemetry handling and legal so we can get a path to a DPA amendment? We are aiming to sign next week.

Thanks,
Samuel Clark
Sr. Privacy Counsel | Brightline Health

Subject: Re: Clarify Redwood's role for telemetry and request for encryption evidence

Samuel — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Aditya (infra) and Priyom (privacy/product) so we can get concrete artifacts. Quick answers up front:

- Role: Redwood considers telemetry that is generated solely to operate and improve the inference service as a "Service Provider" handling Brightline request telemetry; we do not use telemetry for advertising or resale. We can propose DPA addendum language that mirrors the CPRA SP limited-use clause.

- Encryption: We will provide a one-page encryption diagram and a short statement of controls (TLS v1.3 for in-transit, AES-256-GCM at rest, KMS-managed keys with HSM-backed key wrapping).

- Subprocessors: attaching current subprocessor export (redwood_subprocessors_2026-07.csv). For any onshore fallback requests, we have a standard 45-day onboarding plan to stand up an onshore equivalent or arrange onshore caching; timeframe depends on the subprocessor.

Next steps: Aditya / Priyom — can you confirm the encryption artifact and a brief onshore fallback timeline for telemetry handling? Marissa, can you produce a DPA amendment draft that uses SP-limited-use language and includes the fallback commitment? I will send a short email to Brightline legal with the attachments once we have the artifacts.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2026-07.csv

On Mon, Jul 19, 2026 at 10:05 AM kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
> - Encryption: We will provide a one-page encryption diagram and a short statement of controls (TLS v1.3 for in-transit, AES-256-GCM at rest, KMS-managed keys with HSM-backed key wrapping).
>
Adding technical detail for the artifact:

We can produce a one-page diagram (attached: telemetry_encryption_diagram_2026-07.pdf) that includes:
- Network path: client -> API gateway (TLS v1.3) -> inference service (mutual TLS internal) -> telemetry pipeline (Kafka with TLS).
- In-transit: TLS v1.3 for external; mTLS between internal service components.
- At-rest: S3/GCS buckets encrypted with AES-256-GCM; keys stored in AWS KMS with customer master key alias redwood/telemetry; KMS uses HSM-backed key material.
- Access controls: RBAC, least privilege, audit logs (one-year retention by default; extended retention available as an add-on).

Subprocessor onshore fallback note: For telemetry routing vendors we currently use two CDN/edge partners; one has US-only edge options that we can prioritize. Estimated time to switch/truncate offshore telemetry to US-only nodes: ~30–45 days operationally (config + testing). If Brightline requires contractual calendar or a guaranteed SLA, we should capture that in the DPA amendment.

I am attaching the diagram and will follow-up with a short signed statement for legal.

—Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: telemetry_encryption_diagram_2026-07.pdf

Kim / team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. We reviewed the subprocessor list and the encryption diagram. A few final asks before we circulate internally and proceed with the P.O.:

1) DPA amendment: please share the draft DPA amendment (docx) that includes: SP limited-use language, the 45-day onshore fallback commitment for critical telemetry subprocessors, and an explicit reference to the encryption controls (we will need a short statement that is signable by your CTO or security lead).

2) Signed statement: a one-paragraph, signed attestation covering the TLS/AES/KMS details that can be added to the exhibit.

3) Transition plan: for the two named telemetry vendors on the subprocessor list, we need a short runbook (2–3 bullets each) that describes how traffic will be restricted to US-only nodes and how you will validate no offshore cache remains after cutover.

If you can get the DPA amendment and the signed attestation over by EOD tomorrow (2026-07-20), we can meet our internal procurement deadline and issue the P.O.

Thanks — we expect the revision to be mostly templated, so quick turn should be fine.

Regards,
Brightline Health Legal (on behalf of Samuel Clark)
